Lab Exam – part 2 
Academic Year: 2025/2026 
 
1. Business Scenario 
You are a Data Scientist for a leading E-commerce platform. The Marketing department is concerned 
about customer retention. You have been provided with a dataset named "data.xlsx" containing 
customer profiles, satisfaction scores, and transaction summaries. 
Your goal is to build a predictive model to identify customers at risk of churning and provide actionable 
marketing insights. 
2. Dataset 
The file "data.xlsx" includes features such as: 
• CustomerID - Unique customer ID 
• Churn - Churn Flag 
• Tenure - Tenure of customer with the company 
• PreferredLoginDevice - Preferred login device of customer 
• CityTier - City tier 
• WarehouseToHome - Distance in between warehouse to home of customer 
• PreferredPaymentMode - Preferred payment method of customer 
• Gender - Gender of customer 
• HourSpendOnApp - Number of hours spent on mobile application or website 
• NumberOfDeviceRegistered - Total number of deceives is registered on particular customer 
• PreferedOrderCat - Preferred order category of customer in last month 
• SatisfactionScore - Satisfactory score of custom

Academic Year: 2025/2026 
 
1. Business Scenario 
You have been appointed as the Lead Data Scientist for Olist, the largest Brazilian e-commerce 
marketplace. The Marketing Department is planning its budget allocation and loyalty campaigns for 
the upcoming quarter. They need to understand the future value of their current customer base to 
make data-driven decisions. 
Your goal is to build a predictive framework that estimates the Customer Lifetime Value (CLTV) using 
both probabilistic models and machine learning techniques. 
2. Dataset 
You will use the "Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist" (available on Kaggle 
https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce). 
• Focus: You must aggregate the various relational tables (orders, customers, payments, items) 
to create a transactional dataset suitable for CLTV analysis. 
• Timeframe: Define a specific "Calibration" period to train your models and a "Holdout" period 
to validate your predictions.
